lessons.title: Population distribution, density and growth

objectives: Define population density and calculate it
Explain the factors affecting population distribution
Calculate natural increase from birth and death rates
Explain causes and effects of migration
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify that the syllabus uses the same definitions; no real population statistics are given on purpose (use the latest census figures when the teacher adds them).

blocks.md: **Population distribution** shows how people are spread over an area. Some places are crowded and others almost empty. **Population density** is the average number of people living in one square kilometre: density = **population ÷ area (km²)**. Density is only an average: a region may have a crowded town and empty countryside.

blocks.caption: Illustrative population densities
blocks.alt: Bar chart showing three zones with densities of 30, 60 and 90 people per square kilometre; invented figures.

blocks.title: Factors of distribution
blocks.md: People crowd where there is: **fertile soil and enough rain** for farming, **gentle relief**, **water supply**, **jobs** (ports, industries, plantations, administration), good **transport**, and **safety**. Few people live in thick forest, steep mountains, deserts or swamps. In Cameroon the cities of Douala and Yaoundé, the Western Highlands and parts of the north are densely settled; large areas of the forest in the south-east have few people.

blocks.title: Birth rate, death rate and natural increase
blocks.md: **Birth rate** = births per 1000 people per year; **death rate** = deaths per 1000 per year. **Natural increase** = birth rate − death rate (per 1000). To change it to a percentage, divide by 10. Example: birth rate 38, death rate 12: natural increase = 26 per 1000 = 2.6 % a year.

**Migration** is the movement of people from one place to another to live. **Rural–urban migration** means moving from villages to towns. **Push factors** make people leave (poor land, few jobs and services); **pull factors** attract them (jobs, schools, hospitals, a better life). Effects: towns grow fast and become crowded, villages lose young workers, and money is sent home by migrants.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Density uses area, not the number of towns; always check the unit: people per km².
- A high birth rate does not by itself give a fast rise: look at the death rate too.
- Do not call all migration bad: it can bring skills and income as well as problems.

blocks.title: Example 1: density
blocks.statement: A division has 240 000 people and an area of 800 km². Find its population density.

blocks.title: Example 2: natural increase
blocks.statement: A country has a birth rate of 35 per 1000 and a death rate of 9 per 1000. Find the natural increase as a percentage.
steps: The population is growing by 2.6 % a year from natural causes.
